reason: The reflector petals and receiver look like the core parts of the solar furnace, so I’ll try joining them.
expectation: The petals should concentrate sunlight onto the receiver, forming a furnace assembly.

alternatives.reason: Screening the spoil also looks like a useful first step toward feedstock.

effect: The petals cannot join the receiver yet; the result points to steel as their available partner.
reaction: The required intermediate assembly was not obvious.
reason: The failed attempt identifies steel as a compatible partner for the reflector petals.
expectation: The steel should support the reflector petals as part of the furnace assembly.

alternatives.reason: Screening the spoil could advance the feedstock goal instead.

effect: The steel ring supports the reflector petals, leaving the receiver as the apparent next furnace component.
reaction: The braced ring makes the intermediate step physically clear.
reason: The supported reflector should now be able to hold and focus sunlight on the furnace receiver.
expectation: The receiver will join the reflector to form the solar furnace.

alternatives.reason: Screening the regolith could advance the feedstock goal instead.

effect: The receiver completed the solar furnace, leaving the formed feedstock goal.
reaction: The demonstration of concentrated sunlight heating the receiver was satisfying.
reason: The screening mesh looks suited to separating fine material from the excavated regolith for feedstock.
expectation: The mesh will produce screened regolith suitable for further processing.

effect: The mesh needs a steel intermediate rather than combining directly with the regolith.
reaction: Another support step was not obvious from the board.
reason: The compatibility feedback identifies steel as the mesh's available partner.
expectation: The steel will support the mesh as a usable screen.

effect: The steel and mesh made a rigid sieve, which should now separate the excavated regolith.
reaction: The rim and collection tray explain why the mesh needed support.
reason: The completed sieve is suited to screening the excavated regolith for feedstock.
expectation: The sieve will separate fine regolith from larger stones.

effect: The sieve produced screened regolith; it now needs forming to complete the remaining goal.
reaction: Separating the coarse stones makes the feedstock preparation clear.
reason: The workshop press is the obvious place to form the screened material.
expectation: The press will compact the screened regolith into formed feedstock.

effect: The press produced unfired blanks and completed the chapter; pressing shapes the powder but does not give it finished strength.
reaction: The distinction between shaping and firing was a useful detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the solar furnace was worthwhile: the supported reflector and receiver made the concentrated-sunlight heating process tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two failed direct combinations were repetitive; both required a steel support that was not apparent from the initial board.

surprise.text: The pressed blanks remain weak until firing bonds their grains; forming them was not the same as finishing them.

arbitrary.text: The initial need to pair both the petals and the mesh with steel was not obvious, though the resulting ring and sieve rim made physical sense.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the blanks are fired and used; the chapter offered concrete explanations of the making process.
